title: Reopening (1) of the Flexible Framework for Care at Home and Housing Support Services
description: Renfrewshire Council has an existing Flexible Framework ("framework") for the provision of Care at Home and Housing Support Services under the direction of Renfrewshire Health and Social Care Partnership (RHSCP). The framework allows RHSCP to purchase services to support (predominantly older) people to live independently in their own homes for as long as possible with the care and support they need being tailored to them, provided in a tailored and responsive manner. There may also be the occasional requirement for a Renfrewshire Council Children’s Services to arrange support services for a child. The Service is delivered 24 hours per day, 52 weeks per year including public holidays. The size of each individual package of care varies and is dependent on the individual’s assessed needs and outcomes. As the services provided by this framework fall within the ‘Social and Other Specific Services’ category, and it is subject to the procurement regimes set out in section 7, Social and Other Specific Services, both of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015, a flexible approach was designed which allows “new entrants” to apply to be on the framework throughout the duration, as and when determined by RHSCP. RHSCP now wish to reopen the framework to new entrants, to ensure capacity to deliver services across Renfrewshire. The process followed will be the same process used to appoint the original providers. Any tenderer bidding for appointment to the framework will be required to satisfy the same minimum criteria as those awarded a place under the original tender process. INTERESTED PARTIES MUST READ THE Invitation to Tender document FOR FULL DETAILS OF THE MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS FOR THIS FRAMEWORK. - Technical and Professional Ability (2 examples of previous experience of delivering similar services. These MUST be within the last 3 years and demonstrate relevant experience and capacity); - Care Inspectorate Requirements (Registered to deliver a Combined Support Service - Care at Home and a Housing Support Service (or ongoing application for Combined Service); - Care Inspectorate minimum Quality Grade of 3 for all key questions; - SSSC Registration and PVG Checks; - Insurance Requirements; - Financial Standing Requirements; - Health and Safety Requirements; - Cyber Security Requirements. TENDERERS MUST MEET THE MINIMUM CRITERIA, OTHERWISE THEIR SUBMISSION WILL BE EXCLUDED FROM EVALUATION AND THEY WILL NOT BE APPOINTED TO THE FLEXIBLE FRAMEWORK. title: Flow imaging microscope
description: Flow imaging microscope The object of the procurement is a flow imaging microscopy system for morphological analysis and numerical estimation of particles in water (size distribution 2µm – 1 mm) under laboratory conditions. The device must be able to image plankton and other particles in water as color images, calculate indicators related to cell and particle size, pigmentation, color and shape from the images, and enable the easy processing of large sample volumes in a reasonable time. The device must be able to separate phytoplankton cells from other particles using chlorophyll fluorescence and enable the use of fluorescent dyes (FITC). The analytics performed by the device must be able to be monitored in real time to ensure quality control. The device software must support basic analytics and classification of particle data. The device must also be able to be used reliably in field conditions on a research vessel.,

title: Online Questionnaire Management Platform
description: The CITT, supported by the ATSSC, is seeking information from vendors regarding commercially available solutions that could support the administration of questionnaires used by the Trade Remedies Investigations Branch (TRIB). TRIB's questionnaire process is a critical component of trade remedy investigations and includes the development, publication, distribution, collection, validation, management, analysis, and reporting of questionnaire data. The process involves collecting information from Canadian and international stakeholders and requires the secure handling of sensitive information (Protected B) throughout its lifecycle. Protected B is the federal level of security that applies to information and assets that, if compromised, could cause serious injury to an individual, organization, or government. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to gather information on available solutions that can provide a secure, web-based platform for questionnaire management and respondent engagement. The ATSSC is interested in understanding the capabilities, functionality, implementation considerations, security controls, and hosting models available in the marketplace. The desired Online Platform would support the design and management of complex questionnaires, secure respondent access, data collection and storage, reporting and analytics, workflow automation, and e-mail management. The Online Platform must support both internal and external users and provide functionality that promotes efficiency, usability, accessibility, and data integrity. Given the sensitive nature of the information collected by the CITT, the solution must be capable of meeting Government of Canada security requirements, including the protection of Protected B information, data residency within Canada, robust access controls, audit logging, and compliance with applicable Government of Canada cloud and security standards.

Hinnankorotus voi olla enintään 2 % vuodessa. Hinnantarkistusesitys on tehtävä kirjallisesti perusteluineen. Tilaajalla on oikeus hyväksyä tai hylätä esitetty hinnantarkistus. Urakoitsijan tulee vastata tilaajan toimeksiantopyyntöihin yhden (1) työpäivän kuluessa. Tavanomaiset työt tulee aloittaa viimeistään viikon kuluessa tilauksesta, ellei hankekohtaisesti muuta sovita. Kiireelliset työt tulee käynnistää 24 tunnin kuluessa tilaajan pyynnöstä. Asiakirjojen pätevyysjärjestys: 1. Puitesopimus / urakkasopimus 2. Toimeksiantoa koskeva tilaus tai urakkakohtainen sopimus 3. Urakkaneuvottelupöytäkirja 4. YSE 1998 5. Tarjouspyyntö liitteineen 6. Tarjoajan tarjous liitteineen Tilaajalla on oikeus irtisanoa sopimus kuuden (6) kuukauden irtisanomisajalla. Urakoitsijalla ei ole oikeutta irtisanoa sopimusta kesken sopimuskauden ilman tilaajan kirjallista suostumusta. title: Available for Licensing: Fluorescent Tracer Technology for Hydrofluoric Acid Exposure Detection
description: Technology Licensing Opportunity: This technology is available for licensing through Idaho National Laboratory's (INL) Technology Deployment office. INL is not seeking to procure products or services in connection with this technology, and no procurement activity is associated with INL's technology transfer process. Interested parties are invited to contact INL to discuss licensing terms and partnership opportunities. Overview Hydrofluoric acid (HF) is used across petroleum refining, semiconductor manufacturing, glass processing, pharmaceutical synthesis, mineral processing, and laboratory research, among others. Despite established handling protocols, accidental skin or surface contact remains a persistent hazard � compounded by HF's unusual toxicological profile: at low concentrations, early-stage contact produces no pain, burning, or visible irritation, while damage to subcutaneous tissue and bone progresses silently before symptoms appear. This technology introduces a UV-fluorescent tracer additive created froma xanthene powder.. The additive is designed to remain chemically inert while enabling workers to survey skin, clothing, or surfaces using a UV light source after handling. Fluorescence indicates contact, supporting immediate decontamination and first aid before acid penetrates tissue. The approach is intended as a complementary detection layer alongside existing personal protective equipment and engineering controls. Industry Need Current HF safety practice relies on prevention: chemical-resistant PPE, engineered containment, and procedural controls. These measures reduce exposure frequency but do not eliminate the risk of accidental contact, particularly in production environments or during equipment maintenance. No field-deployable method currently exists for workers to confirm the absence of skin or surface contact after an HF-handling task. The standard indicator of exposure is symptom onset, which may occur hours after contact, after significant physiological damage has already occurred. This detection gap represents a structural limitation in current HF safety frameworks across all affected industries. Differentiation and Advantages Post-task detection capability: Designed to enable active worker self-survey after HF handling, a capability not provided by current commercial safety approaches. Chemically inert tracer formulation: Xanthene dye has documented chemical stability in HF environments and is not expected to alter acid reactivity, concentration, or intended function. Early-window treatment support: Detection prior to symptom onset is intended to expand the effective window for decontamination and calcium gluconate application, both of which are more effective when administered early. Leak detection in system processes: Secondarily, this product improves leak detection in industrial processes by creating a high visibility and distinct HF appearance that can reduce detection time and differentiate HF from other clear fluids used in the process. Potential Applications Industrial HF handling operations in petroleum refining, semiconductor etch, glass manufacturing, and pharmaceutical synthesis. Worker post-task self-survey using portable UV light sources following HF-handling tasks. Facility leak and spill detection through UV scanning of work surfaces and equipment exteriors. Laboratory and small-scale research environments where engineering controls may be less robust.

title: DHA - Offsite Sterile Processing Support Services
description: Request for Information (RFI) Defense Health Agency (DHA) Sterile Processing (SP) Offsite Support 1.0 DISCLAIMER: This is NOT a Request for Proposal (RFP) nor a Request for Quotations (RFQ). It is strictly a Request for Information (RFI) and should not be construed as a formal solicitation nor an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. Neither unsolicited proposals nor any other kinds of offers will be considered in response to this RFI, and no contract will be awarded pursuant to this announcement. The information requested by this RFI will be used within DHA to facilitate decision making and will not be disclosed outside of DHA. Any information provided to the Government is strictly voluntary and will be provided at no cost to the Government. 2.0 SUBJECT: The Medical Research and Development Contracting Division 2, Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), is seeking information in the form of capabilities statements and availability. This RFI is for fact-finding and planning purposes only. The information will be used in conducting market research to identify qualified, experienced, and interested potential business sources in support of the Government�s requirements outlined in this RFI, which are subject to change prior to a formal solicitation release. The Government reserves the right to decide whether a small business set-aside is appropriate based on responses to this notice. Contractors are encouraged to inform the Government of any barriers that would prohibit them from competing. Contact with Government personnel, other than those specified in the RFI, by potential offerors or their employees regarding this requirement is not permitted. 3.0 BACKGROUND: The DHA is conducting a Business Case Analysis to identify alternatives to on-site surgical instrument sterilization for Military Treatment Facilities (MTFs) across eight (8) of the nine (9) networks. For more information on the DHA organizational structure see the following link: https://www.dha.mil/Offices-and-Programs/Defense-Health-Networks Sterile processing supports all operating room functions as well as multiple military treatment centers throughout the DHA networks. Sterile Processing Departments (SPD) are the backbone surgical instrument sterilization for MTFs. When SPDs are unusable because of onsite equipment failure, operating room and clinic procedures decrease by greater than 90%, essentially halting the surgical capability of the MTFs. The cessation of surgical cases results in decreased provider readiness, risk of Graduate Medical Education (GME) citation, and severely impacted healthcare delivery. To continue to provide uninterrupted healthcare, the DHA is considering outsourcing a portion SPD service throughout MTFs for service resilience and workload SPD stability. SPD services considered will occur at the contractor�s offsite SPD locations. All companies offering SPD offsite services including healthcare companies and hospitals with capacity to assist with offsite/remote SPD services are encouraged to provide an RFI response. List of equipment to be sterilized may include but is not limited to the following list: � Minimally Invasive Surgical (MIS) Cases (e.g., Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery (FESS), ankle procedures, Sonicision, and punches) � MIS Peel Packs (including dental instrument trays) � All Power Equipment (drills and batteries) � D&C Hysteroscopy � Major Basic Sets � Micro-Laryngeal Instruments (ENT) � ENT General Airway Sets � Arthrex Arthroscopy Shoulder Repair Sets � Arthroscopy Instruments (Arthrex and Stryker) � Abdominal Hysterectomy � Weighted Speculums � Da Vinci Accessories The DHA is seeking industry feedback on contractor�s capabilities to provide offsite sterile processing in support of the following MTFs: � Walter Reed National Military Medical Center, Bethesda, MD (including Naval Postgraduate Dental School and WRNMMC clinics) � Alexander T. Augusta Military Medical Center, Fort Belvoir, VA � Naval Medical Center, Portsmouth VA � Womack Army Medical Center (AMC), Fort Bragg, NC � Evans Army Community Hospital, Fort Carson, CO � Brooke Army Medical Center (BAMC), JBSA Fort Sam Houston, TX � 59th Medical Wing Wilford Hall Ambulatory Surgical (WHASC), Lackland, TX � Carl R. Darnall Army Medical Center (AMC), Fort Cavazos, TX � William Beaumont Army Medical Center (WBAMC), Fort Bliss, TX � 99th Medical Group at Nellis Air Force Base, Las Vegas NV � Naval Medical Center San Diego (NMCSD), San Diego, CA � 60th Medical Group Travis Air Force Base, Fairfield, CA � Army Medical Center (AMC) Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), Tacoma WA � Tripler Army Medical Center (AMC), Honolulu, HI. Critical (no interruptions) locations Winn Army Community Hospital Fort Stewart, GA Martin Army Community Hospital Fort Benning, GA Irwin Army Community Hospital Fort Riley, KS Naval Medical Center Camp Lejeune, NC Naval Hospital Camp Pendleton, CA 10th Medical Group, United States Air Force Academy, CO 4.0 SCOPE: The Medical Research and Development Contracting Division 2, DHACA, is issuing a Request for Information (RFI) to identify Contractors capable of meeting the Government�s requirement. The Government requests a Capability Statement providing the following: 1. General information and technical background describing your firm�s experience in providing similar Sterile Processing (SP) Offsite Support within the last five years, specifically with contracts similar in scope, complexity, and size to meet the program objectives in accordance with this RFI. 2. In your capability statement, address how you would deliver/implement the specific tasks outlined in this RFI. Transportation of surgical instruments between MTFs and offsite facilities. Complete sterile processing services including decontamination, assembly, and sterilization. Personnel to perform the above process. Sterile Processing Facilities Sterile Processing Equipment Inventory Verification Quality Control Verification In your response, please answer the questions on Attachment. 5.0 SMALL BUSINESS SET ASIDE: The Government has not determined the set-aside capability, if possible, at this time. The Government will use the RFI results in analyzing small businesses� capacity to perform this requirement and make its decision. 6.0 RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS: Please submit a Capability Statement and complete the attachment in �.pdf� file type via email to Medical Research and Development Contracting Division 2, DHACA, Contract Specialist Mr. David Daniel david.r.daniel27.civ@health.mil. The subject line of the email should be: �Sterile Processing (SP) Offsite Support � RFI Response.� A vendor responding to this RFI with generic material only, such as brochures, advertisements, or other generic material, is highly discouraged. Maximum participation by small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, HUBZone small business, small-disadvantaged business, and women-owned small business concerns is encouraged. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Parties may begin submitting responses to this request for information immediately. If the information provided contains propriety information, such information must be clearly identified with appropriate disclaimers. All Contractor questions are due NLT 06 October 2026. The Government retains the right to respond to some or all of the questions and group similar questions for a single response. Due date: RFI response submissions are due no later than 11:00 AM (UTC-04:00) Eastern Daylight Time, New York, USA on 30 October 2026. title: Strassenraumgestaltung Obergass- Kirchgass, Eschenbach
description:
Die bestehende 230 m lange Quartiersammelstrasse im Zentrum von Eschenbach ist im Zuge der Sanierung umzugestalten in eine verkehrsberuhigte Strasse. Die Obergass- Kirchgass ist ein stark frequentierter Schulweg . Die Strasse dient als Zufahrt zur Kirche, Friedhof, Schule, Pension Mürtschen und einem Detailhäldner, sowie zu einzelnen Wohnbauten. Die Strasse ist während den Bauarbeiten generell für den Verkehr offenzuhalten. Nur in spezifische dafür vorgesehenen Zeitfenstern sind abschnittsweise Sperrungen möglich (siehe Bauphasenpläne).

Die Stassenentwässerung und Strassenbeleuchtung wird komplett erneuert. Werkleitungsarbeiten für Trinkwasser und Abwasser werden koordiniert erneuert und ausgebaut.

Rohrlegearbeiten für Trinkwasser und Elektroinstallationen für die Beleuchtung sowie Gärtnerarbeiten für die Bepflanzung sind nicht Bestandteil des Auftrags. Die Arbeiten mit den weiteren Arbeitsgattungen sind zu koordinieren. Die Ausführung der Bauarbeiten ist in 8 Etappen geplant.
